PMID:29922066.topic: Supracondylar fracture lateral pin fixation stability
PMID:29922066.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic departments, Hallym Sacred Heart, Haeundae Paik and Severance Children's hospitals (retrospective review)

cycle1.result: Retrospective risk-factor study of lateral-only pinning for Gartland type III fractures; medial comminution in 20 patients (29.8%); pin separation lower with medial comminution (33.8% vs 38.1%, P=0.017); medial comminution associated with Baumann angle change (OR 4.151, 95% CI 1.249–13.800, P=0.020).

PMID:29922066.other_findings: No iatrogenic ulnar nerve injury; all Baumann angle differences were under 10°. Authors recommend an additional medial pin when medial comminution is present.

PMID:32461800.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Kettering General Hospital
PMID:32461800.standard: BOA-endorsed consent guidance (orthoconsent.com); departmental standard of 100% documentation of common, less common and rare risks on Consent Form 1 for NOF fracture surgery

cycle1.result: 2015 cycle: infection 100%, bleeding 87%, clots 93%, anaesthetic risks 53%, neurovascular injury 93%, pain 73%, altered wound healing 60%, non/mal-union 33%, failure of surgery 87%, mortality 40%, prosthetic dislocation 0%, leg length discrepancy 0%.

PMID:32461800.intervention: Verbal and written dissemination of results, printed risk list displayed in the orthopaedic doctors' office, and amendments to the junior doctor induction handbook.

cycle2.result: Of 100 NOF patients, 48 with capacity (AMT ≥8) audited: infection, bleeding, clots and anaesthetic risks 100%; neurovascular injury 98%; failure of surgery 83%; pain 75%; non/mal-union 71%; altered wound healing 69%; mortality 21%; prosthetic dislocation 14%; leg length discrepancy 6%.

PMID:32461800.other_findings: Three cycles (2015, 2016, 2019); 2016 values included anaesthetic risks 76%, pain 42% and mortality 61%. The 100% target was still not met; after the latest cycle the trust approved two consent-specific stickers (arthroplasty/fixation) and inappropriate abbreviations were noted.

PMID:40980789.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital, University Hospitals Dorset (Poole)
PMID:40980789.standard: BOAST ankle fracture guidance; radiological evidence of intra-operative syndesmosis stress testing saved and documented on operation notes, target 80% each

cycle1.result: Radiological evidence saved 55% (n=49); documentation on operation notes 71% (n=63); neither in 25% (n=22).

PMID:40980789.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance; poster in on-call room and theatre areas and a teaching presentation by an associate specialist foot and ankle surgeon.

cycle2.result: Radiological evidence saved 82% (n=41), p=0.001; documentation 82% (n=41), p=0.14; neither in 6% (n=3). Both targets met.

PMID:40980789.other_findings: Audit did not assess the quality or technique of the stress tests, only their presence.

PMID:41466947.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in hip fracture arthroplasty
PMID:41466947.setting: Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:41466947.standard: Trust guideline: three postoperative IV doses of flucloxacillin (teicoplanin if penicillin allergic) after hip arthroplasty for NOF fracture; target 100%

cycle1.result: Postoperative antibiotics given to 150/179 (83.8%), none to 29 (16.2%); 84/121 (69.4%) flucloxacillin recipients completed all three doses; 97/179 (54.2%) fully compliant overall.

PMID:41466947.other_findings: Of 29 with no antibiotics, 12 were mentioned in notes but not prescribed, 8 recorded as not required and 9 not mentioned. Three superficial wound infections (1.7%) and no PJI.

PMID:26734265.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic unit, Monklands District General Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire (emergency admissions)
PMID:26734265.standard: SIGN guideline 122 VTE prophylaxis; seven-item checklist (weight/BMI and eGFR recorded, correct LMWH dose, timely administration, AES prescribed and worn, early mobilisation, hydration), 100% target

cycle1.result: 71% of patients compliant with all measures; errors mainly medical (failure to prescribe LMWH or stockings, incorrect dosing), plus nursing and patient errors; about 30% of surveyed patients (n=47) understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.

PMID:26734265.intervention: Policy of prophylaxis unless contraindicated, summarised guidelines displayed on wards, MDT teaching for doctors and nurses, patient education, VTE added to handover and radiology meeting, teaching after rota change, and VTE education added to junior doctor induction.

cycle2.result: Re-audit 4: 100% compliance; 80% of patients understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.

PMID:26734265.other_findings: Re-audits: 93% (n=27), 100% (n=26), 86% (n=22, dip after medical staff rotation), 100% (n=25); spot audit six months later showed 100%.

PMID:39917097.topic: Preoperative templating radiographs for hip arthroplasty
PMID:39917097.setting: Elective arthroplasty service, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
PMID:39917097.standard: Templating radiographs 7–180 days before THA (New Zealand Orthopaedic Association, South African Arthroplasty Society and GIRFT guidance); goal 100%

cycle1.result: 10/50 (20%) had templating radiographs within 7–180 days; mean 140 days (range 0–788) from latest radiograph to surgery.

PMID:39917097.intervention: Departmental protocol requiring preoperative assessment with templating radiographs, education of NCHDs on radiographs to order, and a departmental rota assigning NCHDs to order them.
PMID:39917097.other_findings: Mean leg length change of 2.26 mm (range 0–17 mm) between radiographs a mean 386 days apart.

PMID:37405130.topic: Paediatric distal forearm fracture ED manipulation (BOAST)
PMID:37405130.setting: Emergency department, district general hospital with paediatric orthopaedic services, Gloucestershire Royal Hospital
PMID:37405130.standard: BOAST early management of distal forearm fractures in children (May 2021): early ED manipulation, neurovascular and consent documentation, orthogonal X-rays, fracture clinic within 7 days

cycle1.result: 23/72 (31.94%) manipulated in ED; 11 of 23 ED manipulations failed.

PMID:37405130.intervention: Local trust pathway in line with BOAST introduced from July 2021 (analgesia/sedation, location, manipulation and referral guidance) with staff education.

cycle2.result: 73/87 manipulated in ED (p<0.00001); 63 (86.31%) acceptable reduction, 10 (13.69%) failed. BOAST compliance: neurovascular documentation pre-manipulation 93.10% (81/87), before discharge 64.36% (56/87); consent documentation 73.56% (64/87); orthogonal X-rays 100% (87/87); fracture clinic within 7 days 49.42% (43/87), mean 8.25 days.

PMID:37405130.other_findings: Reasons for not attempting ED manipulation (14 cases) were not documented; about 63 hours of theatre time saved. Protocol changed so off-ended fractures are manipulated under sedation.

PMID:35959189.setting: Single centre orthopaedic and radiology departments (Leeds Teaching Hospitals affiliation)
PMID:35959189.standard: Local consensus criteria (seven arthroplasty and three radiology consultants): nine criteria for adequate post-operative hip and knee arthroplasty radiographs, four essential

cycle1.result: 69/100 radiographs adequate overall; whole prosthesis and cement visible 86%, relevant anatomy visible 83%, pubic symphysis centred 31%, GT/LT level 32%.

PMID:35959189.intervention: Local guidelines published with radiology, educational and feedback meetings with radiographers, poster in radiography rooms and a quality improvement proforma.

cycle2.result: 84/100 adequate overall; prosthesis and cement visible 93%, relevant anatomy 95%, pubic symphysis centred 47%, GT/LT level 43%; 11/56 (19.6%) hip and 5/44 (11.4%) knee radiographs inadequate.

PMID:35959189.other_findings: Pain score, BMI and number of radiographers were not correlated with inadequate radiographs; exposure fell slightly (95% to 92%).

PMID:39624810.setting: Plastic surgery acute referrals (OARS), Oxford University Hospitals NHS teaching trust
PMID:39624810.standard: BSSH Hand Trauma App guidance and local OUH guidelines on indications for antibiotics in open hand injuries

cycle1.result: 22/44 (50.0%) referrals without an indication were given or advised antibiotics; 10/84 (12%) with an indication were neither given nor advised antibiotics.

PMID:39624810.intervention: Infographic poster displayed and emailed to resident doctors (PDSA 1), then a short microlearning video shared on WhatsApp and email (PDSA 2).

cycle2.result: 5/35 (14.3%) without an indication given or advised antibiotics (p=0.002 vs baseline).

PMID:39624810.other_findings: After the infographic alone (25/7/22–31/7/22, n=52), 7/16 (43.8%) were given unnecessary antibiotics (not significant). Three of the five remaining cases were given antibiotics by the referrer before referral.

PMID:39618767.setting: Tertiary elective orthopaedic hospital, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, London
PMID:39618767.standard: NICE VTE guideline (over 16s): VTE risk reassessment within 24 hours after surgery; target 100%

cycle1.result: 6/4780 (0.13%) had VTE reassessment completed within 24 hours of surgery.

PMID:39618767.intervention: Automated system prompt on EPMA reminding staff to complete VTE reassessment 24 hours after surgery.

cycle2.result: 112/156 (74%) completed within 24 hours (p<0.0001); 131/156 (83%) completed at any time.

PMID:39618767.other_findings: Initial VTE assessment compliance was high because it is a mandatory step on EPMA.

PMID:39233732.setting: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:39233732.standard: NICE hip fracture guidance: sliding hip screw for 31A1/A2 fractures, intramedullary nail for 31A3 and reverse oblique fractures

cycle1.result: Compliance with national guidance on appropriate operation 63% (n=33/52) initially, 73% (n=38/52) after senior review of coding and classification; days to discharge from therapies 8.4 (short nail) vs 11 (DHS), P=0.03.

PMID:39233732.other_findings: 30-day mortality 13% (7/52) overall, higher than the national 5.5%; operating time similar (58.11 vs 58.03 min).

PMID:34712478.setting: Level one trauma centre, trauma and orthopaedics department (Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast affiliation)
PMID:34712478.standard: GMC, RCS Glasgow and BOA consent guidance; no abbreviations on consent forms

cycle1.result: Abbreviations in 189/350 (54%) forms; mostly by registrars (74%); DVT and PE commonest.

PMID:34712478.intervention: Results presented at M&M meeting, email to all staff, reminder sticker attached to consent forms and poster in areas where consent is taken.
PMID:34712478.other_findings: DVT and PE remained the commonest abbreviations; use of CRPS, PIP and EUA rose in proportion.

PMID:38039295.setting: 28 UK hospitals (district general, major trauma and teaching centres)

cycle1.result: Descriptive service evaluation: 50% of injuries considered preventable; commonest injuries single phalanx fracture (15%), wrist fracture (15%), single metacarpal fracture (13%).

PMID:38039295.other_findings: Collected during COVID-19 lockdown; alcohol linked to 1.9% and drugs to 0.54% of injuries.

PMID:35028219.topic: Next of kin involvement in consent for patients lacking capacity
PMID:35028219.setting: 520-bed district general hospital trauma unit (Royal Surrey County Hospital)
PMID:35028219.standard: Mental Capacity Act 2005 best-interests process; documented attempt to contact next of kin before surgery and completion of NoK section of Consent Form Four

cycle1.result: Documented attempt to contact NoK 80% (24/30); NoK section of Consent Form Four completed 30% (10/30).

PMID:35028219.intervention: Feedback presentation at trauma meeting and email to orthopaedic team.

cycle2.result: Documented attempt to contact NoK 100% (28/28), p<0.05; NoK section completed 64.3% (18/28), p<0.05.

PMID:35028219.other_findings: Registrar survey suggested the Consent Form Four NoK section is easily missed; planned consent e-training and form redesign.

PMID:41961322.topic: Ileus after pelvic and acetabular fractures
PMID:41961322.setting: Major Trauma Unit, Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast (Major Trauma Centre)

cycle1.result: Clinically significant ileus 4.12% (4/97); 80.4% (78/97) failed to achieve GI-2 by day 3, mostly due to constipation.

PMID:41961322.other_findings: Length of stay correlated with time to bowel opening (r=0.498, p<0.001); constipation associated with 6.5 days longer stay.
